Scenario playbooks: invoice and refund
These stories reuse the same supervisor, guidance loader, evidence tools, approval gate and case engine.
PROPOSED · 23 NOV 2026
SCENARIO 1 / LIVE E-INVOICE
Najmat: explain a contextual invoice flag and verify its correction
The default invoice is syntactically valid. The issue is the configured tax treatment of selected lines.
Evidence and deterministic checks
Net amount: AED 36,500
VAT charged: AED 525
Configured expected VAT: AED 1,825
Difference: AED 1,300
Buyer registration and line-level check results
Agent tasks and guidance
Load approved invoice-check sections
Explain each finding using its source line
Distinguish format checks from context checks
Draft credit note + replacement invoice
Preserve original and replacement IDs
Approved action and outcome
Visitor approves the exact documents
Send through the illustrative seller app
Ingest and check both correction documents
Verify the new result before reporting success
Expose the same evidence to Inspector
BRANCHES / WHAT YOUR IMPLEMENTATION MUST HANDLE
All checks pass: go directly to completion. Multiple flags: explain each supported finding.
A pending or failed correction stays open. Do not claim the invoice was corrected because a draft exists.
SCENARIO 3 / REFUND EVIDENCE
Al Waha: separate supported, corrected and pending refund components
Evidence collection changes the recommendation; missing e-invoices alone do not determine the result.
Evidence and deterministic checks
Refund claim: AED 284,600
Initially supported: AED 53,600
Further paper-invoice support: AED 150,000
Unsupported and corrected: AED 34,200
Supplier-related amount pending: AED 46,800
Agent tasks and guidance
Retrieve claim breakdown and source records
Load approved evidence-review guidance
Match documents to the amounts they support
Draft a request or decision recommendation
Explain which uncertainty remains unresolved
Approved action and outcome
Visitor approves the demo recommendation
Final supported total: AED 203,600
AED 34,200 corrected / not approved
AED 46,800 remains on hold
Retain the related supplier issue as open
BRANCHES / WHAT YOUR IMPLEMENTATION MUST HANDLE
If documents are insufficient, request further evidence or route for review.
A completed review is different from a fully resolved refund or a closed supplier case.
All amounts and behaviors are from the synthetic demonstration draft. Tax interpretations and action policy require domain-owner approval.
WORKED EXAMPLE / READ FROM TOP TO BOTTOM
Two user conversations with concrete outcomes
Invoice: “Why was it flagged?” Refund: “Why can’t the full claim be supported yet?”
STEP / WHO ACTS
WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DO
WHAT COMES BACK / WHY IT MATTERS
Invoice / Data
Najmat asks about its selected invoice. Retrieve the lines and
configured checks: net 36,500, VAT charged 525, expected VAT 1,825.
Evidence shows a draft VAT difference of AED
1,300. Formatting can still be valid.
Invoice / Explain
Load invoice guidance and explain the affected lines using the
actual check findings. Show the arithmetic: 1,825 − 525.
“The configured checks expect AED 1,300 more
VAT.” Show which lines support it.
Invoice / Act
Draft a credit note and replacement invoice. After approval, send
through the illustrative seller app and check the received
correction records.
Report corrected only after revalidation. If
delivery or checks fail, keep the case open.
Refund / Data
Al Waha asks about its 284,600 claim. Retrieve initial support of
53,600 and pending evidence for the remaining 231,000.
Pending breakdown: 184,200 needs invoice
evidence; 46,800 has a supplier issue.
Refund / Investigate
Review the supplied evidence using approved guidance. It supports
another 150,000; 34,200 remains unsupported and is corrected.
Supported total: 53,600 + 150,000 = AED 203,600.
Refund / Recommend
Prepare the demo recommendation: supported 203,600; corrected/not
approved 34,200; held 46,800. Record the approved outcome.
The three amounts total 284,600. The supplier
case remains open; the review can be complete.
What to remember
Reuse the same agent building blocks, but change the instruction sections, evidence tools and permitted action for each business task.
Worked examples use the supplied synthetic draft. Tool behavior and interfaces are proposed; these are not live taxpayer operations.
